files.lesson.md: --- order: 24 unit: trig9 node: AC9M9M03 n1 uses: [AC9M9SP01 n3] assumes: [AC9M9SP01 n3] connection: tree-height title: Find a side with trigonometry summary: "Name the sides from the angle, pick the ratio that links the side you know to the side you want, then multiply or divide: opposite = hypotenuse × sin, and so on." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "You can't climb the tallest tree in the grounds. You can stand back, measure an angle and work out its height." app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8376 url: http://127.0.0.1:8376/index.html readySelector: "#board" layout: full --- Stand 20 m from the foot of a tall tree. A clinometer (or a phone app) says the top is 40° above your eye level. How tall is the tree? Have a guess before you read on, and we'll come back to it at the end. ## Predict: an easy angle first ```step stage: predict insight: "At 45° the opposite and adjacent sides are equal, so committing to the height shows who sees that tan 45° is 1." check: type: predict q: "Standing 20 m from a tree, the angle up to its top is 45°. How high is the top above your eye level?" options: - "20 m" - "10 m" - "40 m" - "14 m" actual: "20 m. At 45° the opposite side equals the adjacent side (tan 45° = 1). At 40° the height will be a little less." ``` ## Run: sides and angle ```step stage: run insight: "Tangent links the opposite and the adjacent sides: the tree height is the adjacent distance times the tangent of the angle." try: { playground: board, starter: "side.yml#run", height: 560 } check: { type: board, text: "Set $t$ to $40$. Read $\\tan 40°$ from the board.", when: "t = 40" } ``` ## Investigate: choose and calculate ```step stage: investigate insight: "The sides you know and want choose the ratio, and then the calculation is one multiplication or division." tasks: - check: type: number q: "For the tree, opposite $=$ adjacent $\\times \\tan 40°$ with adjacent $= 20$ m and $\\tan 40° = 0.839$. How high above your eye is the top? (1 decimal place)" answer: 16.8 tolerance: 0.1 explain: "20 × 0.839 = 16.78, about 16.8 m." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $20 \\times 0.839$? (1 decimal place)", answer: 16.8, tolerance: 0.1, explain: "20 × 0.839 = 16.78." } - check: type: question q: "You know the adjacent side and want the opposite side. Which ratio do you use?" options: ["Tangent", "Sine", "Cosine", "Any of them"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Sine needs the hypotenuse.", "Cosine needs the hypotenuse.", "Each ratio uses a particular pair."] explain: "Opposite and adjacent: tangent." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#pat" text: "Pat finds the height of the tree. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: trig-divide-instead-of-multiply explain: "Line 3: tan = opposite ÷ adjacent, so opposite = adjacent × tan. Pat divided, which gives a height far too big." ``` ### Find the opposite ```worked \tan 40° = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}} :: The ratio that links the two sides. \text{opposite} = 20 \times \tan 40° :: Multiply both sides by 20. \text{opposite} = 20 \times 0.839 = 16.8 :: Use the calculator in degree mode. \text{opposite} \approx 16.8 \text{ m} :: Above eye level. ``` ### Which ratio ### Find the mistake Read Pat's working. Which line divides when it should multiply? ## Modify: other sides ```step stage: modify insight: "Changing which side is unknown tests the choice of ratio and shows when to divide." tasks: - hint: ["Opposite and hypotenuse: sine.", "opposite = hypotenuse × sin 70°."] check: { type: number, q: "A ladder is $8$ m long and leans at $70°$ to the ground. How high up the wall does it reach? ($\\sin 70° = 0.940$; 1 decimal place)", answer: 7.5, tolerance: 0.1, explain: "8 × 0.940 = 7.52, about 7.5 m." } - hint: ["The unknown is on the bottom this time.", "hypotenuse = adjacent ÷ cos 60°."] check: { type: number, q: "A ramp's horizontal run is $10$ m and it makes $60°$ with the ground. How long is the ramp surface? ($\\cos 60° = 0.5$)", answer: 20, tolerance: 0.1, explain: "adjacent = hypotenuse × cos, so hypotenuse = 10 ÷ 0.5 = 20 m." } - hint: ["Is a 70° ladder steep or shallow?", "The wall height has to be less than the ladder."] check: { type: question, q: "A calculation gives a ladder's reach as $11$ m for an $8$ m ladder. What does that tell you?", options: ["There is a mistake: the height can't be more than the ladder", "The ladder is very steep", "The ladder is long enough", "Nothing: ladders can stretch"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "Even a vertical ladder only reaches 8 m.", "It can't reach further than its length.", "A ladder has a fixed length."], explain: "The opposite side is shorter than the hypotenuse. If it isn't, check for dividing instead of multiplying." } ``` ### Ladder reach ### Ramp length ### Does it make sense ## Practise: find the side ```step stage: practise insight: "Choosing sine, cosine or tangent and then multiplying or dividing." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A triangle has hypotenuse 12 and a 30° angle. The opposite side is hypotenuse × $\\sin 30°$ (0.5). How long is it?" answer: 6 explain: "12 × 0.5 = 6." - check: type: number q: "A cliff is $50$ m high. From the boat the angle up to its top is $35°$. How far is the boat from the foot of the cliff? ($\\tan 35° = 0.700$; nearest metre. Made up for the task.)" answer: 71 tolerance: 1 explain: "50 ÷ 0.700 = 71.4, about 71 m." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $50 \\div 0.7$ to the nearest whole number?", answer: 71, tolerance: 1, explain: "50 ÷ 0.7 = 71.4." } - check: type: number q: "Review: what is the sine of an angle in a triangle with opposite 6 and hypotenuse 10?" answer: 0.6 tolerance: 0.001 explain: "6 ÷ 10 = 0.6." ``` ### Opposite ### Adjacent ### Review ## Make: the tree ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the tree: the angle is measured from eye level, so add the eye height." tasks: - hint: ["The height above eye level is 20 × tan 40°.", "Then add your eye height."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "You stand 20 m from the tree with your eye 1.6 m above the ground. The angle up to the top is 40°. How tall is the tree? ($\\tan 40° = 0.839$; 1 decimal place. The figures are made up for the task.)" steps: - ["opposite $= 20 \\times \\tan 40°$", "the height above eye level"] - ["$20 \\times 0.839 = 16.8$", "multiply"] - ["$16.8 + 1.6 = 18.4$", "add the eye height"] answer: "18.4" answerLabel: "Tree height (m)" tolerance: 0.1 feedback: - ["16.8", "That's above your eye. Add your eye height."] - ["20", "That is the distance, not the height."] criteria: - "I chose tangent because I had opposite and adjacent." - "I added the eye height at the end." - "I gave the answer in metres." explain: "20 × 0.839 = 16.78. Add 1.6 to get 18.4 m." - check: type: question q: "What could make your answer wrong?" options: ["Sloping ground, or a tree that leans", "The tree being tall", "Using a calculator", "Standing 20 m away"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Tall trees are fine.", "A calculator in degree mode is how you do it.", "The distance is one of the measurements."] explain: "The method assumes level ground and a vertical tree." ``` ### Total height ### What could go wrong **Also used in** - **Surveying.** Heights of buildings and cliffs from an angle. - **Aviation.** A plane's height from its distance and angle of climb. - **Next lesson.** Finding the angle when you know the sides. ```teacher summary: Students choose sine, cosine or tangent and use it to find an unknown side, checking the answer makes sense (AC9M9M03, node 1). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 8 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can pick the right ratio for the sides I know and want. - I can multiply or divide to find the side. - I can say if an answer is possible. struggle: "Multiplying or dividing the wrong way. Ask: which side is on top of the fraction?" before: > Students need Sine, cosine and tangent. The one idea: name the sides, pick the ratio, then it's one step. Check the hypotenuse is the longest side. Calculators must be in degree mode: check this at the start. The tree figures are made up for the task. running: - "Predict: show of hands before the board." - "Paper: the tree height in Make is worked on paper first." stuck: - see: A student divides to find the opposite side. ask: Is the unknown on top of the fraction or underneath? fix: "On top: multiply both sides by the bottom." stretch: Measure a real height at school with a phone clinometer app. support: "A printed three-step recipe: name the sides, pick the ratio, calculate." leads: | Continues AC9M9M03 node 1. Where it leads: Finding an unknown angle. exit: q: Opposite = adjacent × ? a: tan of the angle. explain: > Name the sides from the angle, choose the ratio that has the side you know and the side you want, and solve. If the unknown is on top, multiply. If it is underneath, divide. ```

# Pat's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: pat
Adjacent = 20 m, angle = 40°. I want the opposite side.
tan 40° = opposite ÷ adjacent.
So opposite = 20 ÷ tan 40° = 20 ÷ 0.839 = 23.8 m.
# endregion
